newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian stock trading suffers from fuel scarcity.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian stock trading suffers from fuel scarcity.

text.p: Shares closed weaker in thin trading at the Nigerian stock market on Monday as a lingering fuel scarcity showed no sign of easing, dealers said.
The all-share index fell to 8509.32 from 8516.41 on Friday.
The persistent fuel scarcity kept many traders away from work, causing turnover to suffer, dealers said.
"It is becoming almost impossible to do anything with this fuel situation," said one.
Most stocks closed lower. Oil marketer Agip was the worst hit, closing at 18.50 naira, down 50 kobo.
Afribank and Union Bank were down at 6.90 naira and 11.40 naira, losing five kobo and nine kobo respectively.
West African Portland Cement fell five kobo to 62.45 naira and Smithkline Beecham slid two kobo to 5.90 naira.
Food firm Nestle, however, finished stronger on persistent demand at 49.10, up 10 kobo.
Insurer Crusader was also up two kobo at 3.20 naira.
